sections.h2: Boone County offices and where to pay
sections.html:
The Assessor puts a value on each parcel, and the Collector turns that value into a bill and takes the money. The Collector's counter is in Room 118 of the Boone County Government Center, on the southwest corner of Ninth and Ash streets in Columbia. Hours are 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through Friday, and the phone is (573) 886-4285.

Columbia is the county seat, and the Missouri River marks the southern edge of the county. Public schools come from several districts, among them Columbia 93, Southern Boone R-I, Centralia R-VI, Hallsville R-IV, Harrisburg R-VIII and Sturgeon R-V. Each district adds its own levy to the bill, so the statement for your parcel will differ from a neighbor's across a district line.

Boone County has 84,371 housing units for 2025 and an estimated 191,746 residents. Only 57.7 percent of households own their home, which suits a county anchored by the University of Missouri, Columbia College and Stephens College. Sellers here often deal with tenants, investors and out-of-town heirs.

  • Typical home value (2020-2024): $272,800
  • Median household income: $72,758
  • Median gross rent: $1,088 a month
  • New building permits in 2025: 787

The residential assessment rate the Collector lists is 19 percent of market value, and the levy is applied to that assessed figure.

sections.h2: When a Boone County bill must be paid
sections.html:
Payment is due once the bill is in hand, and the hard stop is the last day of the year. The Collector mails statements through November. If yours hasn't shown up by December 10, call the office, because a lost envelope doesn't erase the tax or the penalties.

A mailed check is on time when the postmark reads December 31 or earlier, a rule found in RSMo 139.100. Mail drop boxes sometimes stamp the next day, so mail several days early. In person, a drop box under the shelter at the Ninth Street entrance accepts payments until midnight on New Year's Eve.

After that, late charges grow every month starting in January until the account is cleared. Once a parcel is entered in the back tax book, RSMo 140.100 charges 18 percent of that year's delinquency, or at most 2 percent per month for an owner who redeems ahead of the sale.

Dates run on the same cycle each year. Anyone who misses an appeal window has to watch for next year's notices.

sections.h2: What to do if your assessment looks too high
sections.html:
There are three stages, and you move up one at a time.

  • Contact the Assessor as soon as your notice arrives. A short informal meeting shows how the value was built and settles many disputes.
  • Still unhappy? Complete the Board of Equalization appeal form and send it to the County Clerk. The postmark must fall on or before July's second Monday unless the board extends the date.
  • Take the board's ruling to the Missouri State Tax Commission by September 30 or one month after the decision letter, whichever falls later.

The right to that last step comes from RSMo 138.430. You may also pay under protest. Send the whole bill by year's end with "paid under protest" on the check, then file a written statement with the Collector naming the market value you claim. If you miss the appeal window, the only path left is to challenge next year's number.

The Collector offers a plan covering real estate taxes and Neighborhood Improvement District assessments, and the current bill must be paid before you join. Each month's amount comes from last year's base tax divided by the months remaining, so a plan that begins in March spreads the base across ten payments.

The December installment is trued up to match the actual bill, and the balance must clear by December 31 or the plan can end and late fees apply. You can pay by coupon with cash, check or money order, by bank debit on the 5th or 20th, or by credit card on the 20th with 2.3 percent added.

Where a lender collects tax money along with the mortgage payment, the lender requests the bill and pays it. If the request came before October 1, the owner gets an informational statement showing that the lien holder asked for it. A statement without that note should go to the mortgage company right away.

Responsibility stays with the owner, though. Unpaid real estate bills collect penalties after December 31 even when a servicer was meant to pay, so if you have a new servicer or a loan that was just paid off, verify where the bill is going. Owners without escrow can pay directly from the informational statement.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax after a sale closes?
sections.html:
The buyer inherits it. Tax is a lien riding with the real estate, so a new owner answers for any unpaid balance. Buyers pay the full bill by December 31, the parties usually prorate by months or days owned, and no tax money goes to the Collector on closing day.

Watch the calendar on closings from October 1 onward. The bill may still be printed under the seller's name and sent to the old address unless the buyer reports the new ownership to the Collector or Assessor. A seller who receives a bill for a house already sold should pass the buyer's name and mailing address to the Collector.

For back taxes, RSMo 140.150 lets an owner pay the delinquent tax, penalty and costs to the Collector right up to the moment of sale. A cash buyer faces the same lien rule, so a clean payoff before closing helps any kind of sale move quickly.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Boone County property tax?
faqs.a: December 31. A payment in hand or postmarked by then avoids charges. Bills go out during November, and charges build each month from January.

faqs.q: Where can I pay in person?
faqs.a: Visit Room 118 of the Boone County Government Center in Columbia between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM on weekdays. A drop box at the Ninth Street entrance accepts payments until midnight on December 31.

faqs.q: Does the county auction tax certificates?
faqs.a: Yes. The annual sale takes place on the fourth Monday of August at 10:00 AM on the courthouse steps and covers real estate with unpaid taxes.

faqs.q: When is the Board of Equalization deadline?
faqs.a: The second Monday of July each year, unless the board extends it. Miss it and the next chance comes with the following year's assessment notices.

faqs.q: Do I owe the tax if I never received a bill?
faqs.a: Yes. A missing bill doesn't release the owner from the tax or the late fees. Call (573) 886-4285 if nothing has arrived by December 10.
